column3: Nearly identical warning: obedience to a group outside faith can reverse believers after faith.
Shows people being turned away from divine signs, without the focus's obedience or loss sequence.
Sets obedience to God and the Messenger against turning away and disbelief.
Closely parallels the prohibition on turning back and the outcome of becoming losers.
Locates a battlefield turning-away among believers and names a contributing cause.
States the positive command to obey God and the Messenger, already established by closer cards.
Adds only the result of deeds failing and becoming losers.
Hidden treachery is not linked here to obedience, reversal, or loss.
Uses an irreversible return idiom for punishment, not the focus's moral reversal.
Portrays turning back on heels when divine signs are recited.
Trustworthiness toward some People of the Book does not clarify the focus's warning.
Contrasts obedience to the Messenger with turning away and assigns responsibility to each side.
Preserves the opposing claim that following a messenger causes loss, exposing a contrary pressure.
A return of sight is unrelated to turning back from faith.
Return to God and an invalid call do not illuminate the warning about obedience.
Supplies the broad outcome of being losers without the focus's causal path.

Gives an explicit prohibition against obeying corrupt excess-makers.
Shows battlefield failure, dispute, and disobedience as a nearby account of reversal in the same setting.

The battle contrast with disbelievers lacks the focus's obedience-to-reversal relation.
A family pledge does not bear on the warning.
Distinguishes willing from compelled outward compliance, only indirectly relevant to obedience.
Pairs obedience and turning away with divergent outcomes, though in a different call.
The battle scene does not develop the focus's warning beyond shared opposition.
Describes a trustworthy one who is obeyed, a general positive contrast without reversal.
Forbids intimate alignment with enemies who reject the truth, supplying a related boundary of loyalty.
Divine turning away of temptation is not the focus's human obedience relation.
A repeated prophetic call to obey is redundant after earlier direct obedience cards.
Keeps obedience to God and the Messenger meaningful even amid an unsettled profession of faith.
The narrative accusation has no relevant obedience or reversal relation.
The return of hostile forces frustrated is not a believer's turning back.
Warns believers against adopting disbelievers' counterfactual talk after battle, a contextual social caution.
Irreversible divine punishment is a different use of return/repelling language.
Commands obedience and warns against turning away, though it repeats the guidance already supplied.
Prohibits cooperation in sin and aggression, adding a neighboring limit on shared action.
Following God's path under repentance is positive orientation, but not a close parallel.
This repeated prophetic command adds no distinct understanding beyond earlier repetitions.
Companions beautify what lies before and behind people, depicting a social mechanism of misdirection.
Prior worship obstructs one person's response, without the focus's obedience-to-disbelievers pattern.
A further identical prophetic command is redundant.
Explicitly describes persistent efforts to turn believers back from their religion and the resulting loss.
The accusation of ill omen does not address the focus's warning.
Returning horses is unrelated to moral reversal.
Contrasts following the Messenger with turning back on one's heels.
The king's dream request offers no relevant relation.
Names a desire among People of the Book to turn believers back to disbelief after faith.
The non-repelling of divine harm is not the focus's turning back.
Divine protection from evil is a remote contrary pattern of being turned away from wrong.
This repeated prophetic command is redundant.
Prohibits giving one's back to disbelievers in battle, making the reversal image concrete.
Shows believers weighing down toward the earth when called forth, a related reluctance rather than obedience to disbelievers.
Gives the favorable communal destination of obeying God and the Messenger, already well covered.
Requires verification of a corrupt person's report, a safeguard against being led into harmful action.
Contrasts a sound foundation with a compromised place, only generally relevant to choosing alignment.
This repeated prophetic command is redundant.
Promises firm footing to believers who support God, a constructive counterpoint to turning back.
Presents committed believers as not seeking exemption from struggle, a distant contextual counterpart.
This repeated prophetic command is redundant.
The offered saving trade does not clarify obedience to disbelievers or reversal.
Depicts doubting hearts wavering, a possible condition of susceptibility but not the stated warning.
Preserves the distinction between inability and turning away while affirming obedience in other capacities.
Shows disbelievers turning back defeated, an opposite battlefield reversal with a distinct agent.
An excuse about trial does not develop the focus's obedience relation.
Pairs hearing with obedience as a positive communal response, but is redundant.
Divorce procedure has no relevant connection.

The fasting command does not add to the focus.
A marital return right is unrelated to reversal from faith.
Warns that hostile dominance may return people to its religion, ending in failure.

Forbids taking even close kin as allies when they prefer disbelief over faith.
Inability to endure patiently is unrelated to the focus's obedience warning.
The command to remember God does not clarify the focus.
Inability to retrieve water is unrelated to moral obedience.
Household-entry etiquette does not bear on the warning.
Exposes false claims of refusing obedience in an alliance with disbelievers, only indirectly relevant.
Bounds obedience to delegated authority by returning disputes to God and the Messenger.
The barrier's resistance to attack is unrelated to obedience.
Bare denial by disbelievers adds no specific relation.
Connects the Messenger's authority to obedience and a route back after wrongdoing.

Blessing the Prophet is not a relevant obedience or reversal pattern.
Return to frail old age is unrelated to the focus.
The compensation rule does not illuminate obedience or reversal.

A domestic obedience condition is a different relation and adds little to the focus.
Mercy after excess does not clarify the warning.

The disputed accusation about violence has no relevant relation.

The arrival of a clarifying messenger does not add to the focus.
Shows that the Messenger must not be made to obey the community, preserving proper direction of guidance.
Pilgrimage rules do not bear on the warning.
Explicitly depicts a concealed promise of partial obedience to those who hate revelation.
Names pressure to follow another religious community's way, directly sharpening the focus's external-obedience warning.
Warns against following others' desires after knowledge, a parallel to abandoning received direction.
Preserves the appeal to inherited following even against guidance and reason.
Forbids following Satan's footsteps, naming an alternative path of incremental misdirection.
Immediately counters the focus's feared allegiance by naming God as the believers' protector and helper.
Depicts fleeing in battle while the Messenger calls from behind, extending the focus's reversal into its immediate scene.
Records a disbelieving claim that compliance with them would have prevented death, exposing rival battlefield counsel.
Forbids fear of Satan's allies and redirects fear to God, clarifying a pressure behind obedience to hostile forces.
Shows recourse to false authority despite a command to reject it, with Satan seeking far misguidance.
Portrays hypocrites turning away when summoned to God and the Messenger.
Makes submission to the Messenger's judgment a test against inward resistance.
Defines obedience to the Messenger as obedience to God, clarifying the authorized direction of obedience.
Links opposing the Messenger and following a path other than believers' to decisive departure after guidance.
Forbids following desires away from revealed judgment, a direct alternative to being led by others.
Explicitly warns that following others' desires may turn one away from part of what God revealed.
Forbids taking those who mock the religion and disbelieve as allies, a close loyalty boundary.
Forbids following desires of people who strayed and led many others astray.
Warns that obeying the majority on earth can lead one away from God's way.
States that obedience to whispering allies would make believers join their association, an exact obedience-to-deviation relation.
Commands following the single straight path and forbids other paths that divide from it.
Commands following what was sent down and forbids following other protectors besides God.
Shows one who casts off signs and follows desire, a personal mechanism of departure from guidance.
Commands believers to obey God and the Messenger and not turn away while hearing.
Calls believers to respond to God and the Messenger when summoned to what gives life.
In the battle setting, joins obedience to God and the Messenger with steadfastness and forbids divisive dispute.
Marks disbelievers as allies of one another, contextualizing the boundary against yielding to their direction.
Questions whether believers will take intimates apart from God, the Messenger, and believers.
Sets attachment to family, wealth, and homes against God, the Messenger, and striving when loyalties conflict.
Depicts religious authorities being taken as lords, a caution about misplaced obedience.
Describes hearts of some believers nearing deviation during hardship and God's turning toward them.
Preserves the appeal to ancestral following against a new message.
States that Pharaoh's people followed his command and that his command was not rightly directed.
Forbids inclining toward wrongdoers, a broad boundary against alignment with them.
Has Joseph leave the way of a people who disbelieve, framing departure from an unbelieving social path.
Records disbelievers threatening to return messengers and followers to their religion or expel them.
Portrays followers confronting leaders whom they followed without receiving relief.
Has Satan acknowledge that he called and people responded, distinguishing invitation from compelled power.
Warns that a foot may slip after being firm through diverting from God's way, closely echoing reversal.
Describes an attempt to turn the Messenger away from revelation through pressure to fabricate another message.
Shows the near possibility of inclining toward that pressure absent divine firmness.
Forbids obeying one whose heart is heedless, who follows desire, and whose affair is excess.
Warns against someone turning a person away from the Hour through desire.
Pairs following the prophet with obeying his command against contrary communal conduct.
Promises freedom from going astray to those who follow divine guidance.
States that if truth followed people's desires, the heavens and earth would be corrupted.
Explicitly commands not obeying disbelievers and instead striving against them with the Qur'an.
Forbids obeying parents when they exert pressure to associate others with God.
Records disbelievers inviting believers to follow their way while falsely offering to bear the consequences.
Again forbids obedience to parents in pressure toward association while retaining good companionship.
Preserves the appeal to follow ancestral practice instead of what God sent down.
Directly commands the Prophet not to obey disbelievers or hypocrites.
Commands following revealed guidance and leaving reliance on other direction to God.
Denies believers an independent choice once God and the Messenger have decided a matter.
Repeats the command not to obey disbelievers or hypocrites and to disregard their harm.
Shows people wishing they had obeyed God and the Messenger rather than the path they took.
Attributes being led astray to obeying leaders and great ones.
Commands following those who seek no payment and are rightly guided, a positive test for whom to follow.
Forbids serving Satan and identifies him as an open enemy.
Depicts people finding ancestors astray yet racing after their tracks.
Forbids following desire because it diverts from God's way.
Praises those who avoid false authorities and turn to God, a constructive alternative to their obedience.
Commands steadfastness and forbids following others' desires.
Records reliance on ancestors' way as claimed guidance.
Shows each community's leaders appealing to inherited practice against a messenger.
Describes Satan being assigned as a close companion to one who turns from God's remembrance.
States that such companions turn people from the path while those people think themselves guided.
Commands following the revealed law and forbids following desires of those without knowledge.
Contrasts disbelievers following falsehood with believers following truth from their Lord.
Describes people turning back after guidance while Satan entices and extends hopes.
Links following what angers God and hating what pleases Him to the ruin of deeds.
Forbids believers from putting themselves ahead of God and the Messenger in direction and judgment.
Warns believers not to become like those whose hearts hardened over time after receiving scripture.
Shows Satan taking control, causing forgetfulness of God, and forming his party.
Sets Abraham's community's disavowal of disbelief as a model of loyalty boundary.
Commands obedience to God and the Messenger while limiting the Messenger to clear delivery.
Directly commands not obeying deniers.
Continues the prohibition against yielding to a contemptible habitual oath-maker and corrupter.
Has Noah complain that his people disobeyed him and followed those whose wealth and children increased only loss.
Directly commands not obeying the obstructer, with prostration and nearness as the contrary response.
